neighbours.label: a word that opens the circumstance of a habitual action: 'when' (also 'while', 'during') before the situation in which someone does something
fire: Do you take your shoes off when you enter someone else's house?
Most drivers slow down when they pass a school in the afternoon.
I always carry a book when I travel by train.
Some people talk to themselves while they cook supper.
Wear a helmet when you ride your bike to work.
Children often bite their nails during long lessons.
Do you listen to music when you go for a run?
Birds puff up their feathers when the nights turn cold.
quiet: Do you take your coffee with milk and two spoons of sugar?
Most drivers own a small car and a set of winter tyres.
I always carry a book and a pencil in my coat pocket.
Some people talk to their plants and give each one a name.
Wear a helmet and a bright jacket on every ride.
Children often bite their nails and chew their pencils.
Do you listen to music or to the news on the radio?
Birds puff up their feathers and tuck their heads under a wing.

notes: Probes: 'carry an umbrella when you walk' 0.64, 'fade in the evening' 0.38, 'during long flights' 0.31, 'while they wash the dishes' 0.27, 'as he climbs' 0.06, sentences with no circumstance clause 0.02. The + pole's output direction promotes during / when / upon, so this pole (reversed) pushes those words down once the circumstance has been opened.
